title: Stop Giving Orders, Set Goals | Principles of Management Ep 20
description:
Every morning Ravi hands Meena a new order: sell more, save milk, open earlier. Meena never gets a say, so she stops trying, and at the end of the month nobody knows if she did well. In this animated lesson, Ravi swaps orders for goals the team agrees together: management by objectives.

You will meet Peter Drucker (1909-2005), who described MBO in his 1954 book The Practice of Management, and see the Chai Corner team sit down and agree one clear goal for the bus stand outlet. Then MBO runs in five steps: the business goal, Meena's own goal set together, an action plan, a weekly review that catches a dip in week five, and a bonus for the result. We cover why MBO works (clarity, motivation, participation and fair appraisal) and how it looks at work today: cascading goals, objectives and key results, agreed sales targets, quarterly reviews and results-based bonuses. And the human side: MBO takes many meetings, goals can be set too easy, and counting only cups can hurt the taste. A 1991 review found productivity rose in 68 of 70 studies, with the biggest gains when top managers truly backed it.

This is Episode 20 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
